preamble: Hardening of the palatal glide [j] to the voiceless palatal stop [c] is the 'glide hardening' of Cypriot Greek: where a consonant is followed by prevocalic /i/, Cypriot has an obstruent, [c] after /p t f v θ ð/ (with devoicing of a preceding voiced consonant) and [k] after /ɾ/. The glide analysis follows Newton (1972) and Kaisse (1992), in which /i/ first becomes [j] before a vowel and the glide is then replaced by the stop; Arvaniti (2010) describes the same facts as /i/ alternating with a palatal or velar stop.

examples.note: The glide surfaces as [c] and devoices the preceding /v/ to [f].
The glide hardens to [c]; the geminate simplifies to conform to Cypriot phonotactics.
The glide hardens to [c] after /f/; the geminate fricative simplifies.
